title: SE quick fallback matrix & cost-latency microflow (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A 6-slide rapid-play deck for SEs to: 1) qualify performance-sensitive inference requests quickly, 2) map to the right Redwood deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), and 3) run the quick fallback checks when latency or cost concerns arise. This is a working sketch — focus is speed for customer calls.

Audience:
- Sales Engineers (pre-sales)
- Platform architects evaluating migration from cloud-hosted endpoints
- AEs who need a 3-min technical primer during exec calls

Slide 1: 30s framing + decision trigger
- One-liner: "Pick the mode that meets your SLO, cost target, and compliance needs — we help you test the tradeoffs in <48h"
- Quick triage knobs (checkbox): expected qps, p95 latency target, regulatory data constraint, average prompt length (tokens), peak burst pattern
- If p95 < 200ms -> note: consider Dedicated with low-latency kernel profile or Hosted with regional routing + cache priming

Slide 2: Fallback matrix (human-friendly)
- Columns: "Problem observed" | "Immediate SE probe" | "Likely root" | "Quick fallback"
- Example row A: "p95 spikes on long-context dialogs" | "Check model seq length & KV cache hits (use trace header)" | "KV-warmup misses or wrong batching" | "Enable prefix caching, lower batch target, route to higher-memory instance"
- Example row B: "Cost per 1k tokens higher than expected" | "Confirm model flavor (quantized?) + tokenization mismatch" | "Using full float model; prompts include heavy system/context" | "Switch to quantized flavor for throughput, add response length cap, suggested cost delta + example numbers"

Slide 3: Quick config scripts for SEs (copy-paste snippets)
- Mini-checklist that SEs run in console:
  - Verify model variant: model:rw-v1-small-quant (if >= 90% quality acceptable)
  - Check routing policy: region=us-west, fallback=rw-v1-medium
  - Inspect recent traces: search trace_id in console -> percent KV hits
- Rapid commands (pseudocode):
  - curl -X POST /v1/trace/query -d '{trace_id: <id>}'
  - Console path: Console -> Models -> Selected model -> Perf profile -> last 24h

Slide 4: Cost vs latency envelope (one-slide ROI)
- Simple unit economics: per-1M tokens examples (hosted vs dedicated reserve vs private on-prem infra). Provide ballpark multipliers and a small table: hosted baseline, dedicated per-token effective, private (capex + ops) rough amortized number.
- Visual note: where caching and batching move you along the curve (arrows: caching -> lowers cost at same latency; batching -> lowers cost but increases tail latency)

Slide 5: Objection handling snippets (SE script)
- "We need <100ms p95": ask about avg prompt length, concurrency pattern. Offer canary: Dedicated small fleet with 99.9 SLA for 2 weeks.
- "We can’t expose data to cloud": clarify VPC/private deployment options + HSM/KMS integration note and link to compliance sheet.
- "Quantization will break quality": propose A/B eval with sample prompt set; show acceptability threshold (e.g., 95% pass on key prompts).

Slide 6: Call checklist + next steps
- On-call checklist for a live demo: warm KV cache (provide simple script), pre-warm tokens by replaying representative prompts, set safety net routing (hosted->dedicated fallback), enable short TTL caching for rapid iterations.
- Next steps: run 48h performance probe with metrics we need: p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, KV hit rate, per-token cost estimate.

Working notes / TODOs (internal):
- Add actual per-1M token numbers from the pricing team (ask @Samir for latest reserved-capacity rates).
- Confirm tooling snippets are copy/paste-ready from Console (Jordan to verify exact curl endpoints).
- Build a 1-slide version for AE "elevator summary" (<= 30s script).
- Create a follow-up play for migration from managed endpoints to Dedicated with migration checklist (data export, model pinning, traffic cutover steps).

Open questions to resolve with engineering before finalizing:
- Can we surface KV hit-rate easily via the public trace API? (engineering/observability task)
- Exact latency delta when enabling prefix caching on rw-v1-large (perf team measurements requested)
- Documented quantization quality deltas across typical enterprise prompt sets

Slack & refs: 
- Slack thread: #se-battlecards-thread-2025-11 (has raw call transcripts to extract sample prompts)
- Jira: GT-3421 = SE fallback matrix epic
- Confluence draft: SE Fallback Matrix (link in metadata)

Notes to self: Keep language light, avoid heavy ops detail in AE version. This deck is an SE tool — include copyable commands and rapid numbers. Want one quick button: "Start 48h probe" that populates the checklist in Console (ask devteam if doable).

End of draft.
